head: f1890ff66d8d9c6fb77c42d805899bbc8faa2b28
restatement_without_rationale: A completion source ID F 2 is accepted and then its inline marker does not become a citation chip.
method: Independent fresh static refutation against actual committed parser, producer and renderer before edits/tests.

refutation_attempts.counterexample: Could the boundary reject whitespace inside source IDs?
refutation_attempts.result: No. /^f\s*[1-9]\d*$/i explicitly accepts it; duplicate/reference checks remove whitespace, then citations.push stores raw n.

refutation_attempts.counterexample: Could the rail or renderer normalize source IDs later?
refutation_attempts.result: No. Rail forwards citations unchanged. injectCitationMarkers keys source IDs by uppercase only, while answer markers remove whitespace and uppercase. F 2 therefore cannot match normalized F2.

refutation_attempts.counterexample: Could current server numeric-only final IDs make this outside the boundary contract?
refutation_attempts.result: No. Current resolver emits numeric final IDs, but the explicit external-network/older-revision frontend contract deliberately accepts F string forms. Every admitted form must be usable downstream.

minimal_fix: Store validated string citation IDs with whitespace removed, preserving their case. Keep numeric IDs unchanged; retain existing normalized comparison, duplicate checks and answer-literal contract.
proof_plan: Extend the existing stream owner with uppercase/lowercase spaced IDs; feed the actual admitted payload to the existing shared renderer and assert its chip callback receives the canonical source for both marker variants while unmatched numeric literals remain literal.
limits: Wire/render identity consistency does not establish source faithfulness.
No backend, prompt, model, scorer, endpoint, lifecycle or shared-renderer changes required.
